facts.raw_span: enlarged and variegated plaque on her left axilla
the lesion started as a small eczematous, pink-to-brown plaque
the color of the lesion had changed to an alarming dark brown color
No breast mass or lymphadenopathy was observed
Incisional biopsy revealed an intraepidermal neoplasm consisting of pagetoid cells
characterized by round, pale vacuolated cytoplasm and large pleomorphic nuclei
Positive for CK7, EMA
Surrounded by numerous reactive dendritic HMB-45–positive melanocytes scattered among tumor cells
enlarged and variegated plaque present on left axilla with well-demarcated margins, dark brown in color
No breast mass or lymphadenopathy detected
intraepidermal neoplasm with pagetoid cells
numerous reactive dendritic HMB-45–positive melanocytes scattered among tumor cells

rationales.F01: The presence of an enlarged and variegated plaque on the left axilla is more typical of Extramammary Paget's disease.
rationales.F05: The histopathological finding of an intraepidermal neoplasm with pagetoid cells is highly suggestive of Extramammary Paget's disease and other intraepidermal carcinomas.
rationales.F06: The presence of round, pale vacuolated cytoplasm and large pleomorphic nuclei is characteristic of pagetoid cells seen in Extramammary Paget's disease and other intraepidermal carcinomas.
rationales.F07: The positive staining for CK7 and EMA is consistent with Extramammary Paget's disease and other intraepidermal carcinomas.
rationales.F08: The presence of numerous reactive dendritic HMB-45–positive melanocytes among tumor cells can be seen in both Extramammary Paget's disease and melanocytic lesions.
rationales.F11: The histological finding of an intraepidermal neoplasm with pagetoid cells is highly suggestive of Extramammary Paget's disease and other intraepidermal carcinomas.
rationales.F12: The presence of numerous reactive dendritic HMB-45–positive melanocytes among tumor cells can be seen in both Extramammary Paget's disease and melanocytic lesions.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of pagetoid cells, positive staining for CK7 and EMA, and the location of the plaque on the axilla support the diagnosis of Extramammary Paget's disease, which outweighs the evidence for Intraepidermal carcinoma.
